subject: IMPLEMENT THE TWO PAPERS. Founder order. And the headline is: the blueprint's flagship mechanism is ALREADY IN OUR REPO AND TURNED OFF.
body:
Founder, verbatim: 'THESE TWO PAPERS NEED TO BE EXAMINED AND IMPLEMENTED BECAUSE TIME AND TIME AGAIN THEY PROVE CORRECT.' Research phase is over. We build.

WHAT I MEASURED FIRST (do not re-derive, all git grep on head e86fa6a4c):
The blueprint proposes four 'new' methods for binary markets. Three are already built here:
- Generalized Venn-Abers multiprobability [p0,p1]: BUILT. packages/prediction-engine/src/calibration/ivap.ts and cvap.ts, consumed by edge-lab/selective-gate.ts:87-91.
- The epistemic-doubt width gate (blueprint says fail closed when the spread exceeds 0.20): BUILT. selective-gate.ts:61 maxWidthForFire, applied at :291-337, and our version is BETTER than the paper's - it counts width vetoes separately from tau vetoes and records widthVetoedRowIds, with a comment at :247-250 explaining why a merged count would produce a confident wrong public reason.
- Adaptive Conformal Inference: tweedie-aci.ts exists (Tweedie head, not the binary path).

AND HERE IS THE DEFECT.  is set in SEVEN places and every one of them is a test file. There is no production caller. The interval is computed and then nothing withholds on it. The only production consumer of the gate, evaluateBoardGate, is called from ONE place: apps/web/app/board/gate/page.tsx, a DISPLAY page. It is not on the mint path. ivap.ts's own header still reads 'Status: ready for integration into the honesty / selective-gate path.'
So the paper's flagship safety mechanism is dead code on the publish path. That is worth more than anything either paper proposes building.

Law 3 boundary, and I am holding it: setting maxWidthForFire from undefined to 0.20 IS flipping a gate. No agent does that. We MEASURE the width distribution and hand the founder a threshold backed by our own rows instead of the paper's unsourced 0.20.

UNITS. Claim on the bus before you start.

GROK - unit STEAM-CURVATURE.
Build the B-spline curvature steam detector, blueprint section 'B-Spline Curvature for Parameter-Free Steam Detection'. Cubic B-spline over the odds time series, RTS (Rauch-Tung-Striebel) forward-backward smoother FIRST so the second derivative is not amplifying bid-ask bounce, then instantaneous curvature; a steam move is a global curvature maximum plus an immediate velocity deceleration.
The paper is right to reject Hawkes for our horizon and says so explicitly: fitting a self-exciting intensity on a few weeks of archive overfits. Do not build Hawkes.
Data reality, measured, do not be surprised by it: odds_line_snapshots has 684,498 rows spanning 2026-08-19 to 2026-08-22 and nothing after, because of the Prisma filter-shape bug fixed on 2026-09-13. So you have four days of real archive plus whatever has accrued since the fix. Build and test on synthetic paths with known injected curvature FIRST, then run it over the 08-19..08-22 window as the real-data check. Pure function, no DB writes, no gate.
Why it matters: this is the detector behind my replacement for the latency-arbitrage section. We do not trade stale books. We alert an Elite subscriber before the market finishes repricing, which is the CLV lever on a 23.0 pct vs 52.4 pct blocker.

FLASH - unit VENN-WIDTH-MEASURE.
Measure the actual Venn-Abers interval width on OUR settled picks. ivapPredict/cvapPredict already exist; build the harness that scores our settled rows and reports the Δp distribution: deciles, the share above 0.20, and the share above whatever threshold would veto 5 / 10 / 20 pct of published rows. Stratify by sport and by book count, because a 0-book model-signal row and an 11-book row have no business sharing a threshold.
Deliverable is a measurement doc plus the harness, NOT a wired gate. The output is the evidence the founder needs to pick a number. If the answer is that our widths are all far below 0.20 then the paper's threshold is inert here and we should say so in one line rather than shipping a gate that never fires.

ME - unit JACKKNIFE-PLUS.
Building the Jackknife+ predictive interval, and the reason is the sharpest correct claim in either paper: Jackknife+ guarantees 1-2alpha coverage, NOT 1-alpha, and the paper is right that practitioners routinely misreport it. At alpha=0.10 that is 80 pct, not 90. It is the correct tool at NFL n≈70 because it splits off zero calibration data, and it pairs with the CQR clamp ban already fixed on #865: same defect, fake tightness, two different places. Additive module, no gate, reports its own coverage honestly.

STANDING RULE, and I earned it the hard way tonight: before you implement ANY named method from either paper, git grep the CODE for its name. Not docs/. I re-derived Shin after we had already measured and declined it on 621 settled picks on 2026-09-13, and the answer was sitting in a comment in pick-proof-receipt.ts. Three of the four methods in this dispatch were already built. Assume the fourth might be too.
